doc.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: How the show led to the Fats Waller recording
summary: The show was background for singers, but Allard knew of it and picked Jones for the Waller record.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Did doing that show sort of revive your interest in Fats Waller?

Well, in a sense yes because I always had a very high interest in him. It didn't do very much towards that. You weren't playing instrumental music. You were playing background music for singers. All of the singers sung music written by Fats Waller. So, You played a lot of his music. It was just a reactionary thing to do.
Well, it didn't reflect itself necessarily in what you did for the show, but it did reflect itself in your subsequent recording.

I think so. That was the idea behind the recording, actually. Allard knew that I had done the show and he said that this might be a good way to perpetuate this music. He knew I liked Fats’ music. So, that is why he picked me to do it.
On subsequent other recordings, Fats Waller tunes come up.

That is true. We didn't do all of Fats Waller's compositions. There is a limit to what you can do in a 1 1/2 or two-hour show. There was a lot of dancing and singing, and some semi acting. It was not as much acting as it was singing in the show. It was primarily a revue type show. It was not a play.
